scenario.summary: The agent-framework PyPI package (versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2) was compromised to include a persistent credential stealer triggered by a .pth startup hook. The malware executes in the background of any Python process to harvest cloud tokens, environment variables, and configuration files from the filesystem and process memory for exfiltration to webhook.site.

meta.hypothesis: An intruder has installed a compromised version of the agent-framework package which persists via a .pth hook and harvests cloud credentials by reading environment variables from the /proc filesystem and local configuration files.

hunt.name: Malicious Python Package Persistence and Secret Theft
hunt.description: This hunt identifies hosts impacted by the agent-framework supply-chain compromise. The malicious versions (1.26.1 and 1.26.2) use a .pth startup hook to execute a credential stealer every time any Python script starts. The stealer forks a background process to harvest environment variables from up to 300 running processes and searches for Azure, AWS, and GitHub credential caches on disk. We trace the lifecycle from package installation and hook creation to active secret harvesting behavior.
